summary: Fixed the v0.14.12 (S3f2658) claude-tui reattach startup deadlock: spawnWithArgs fed the ATTACH replay into the emulator BEFORE starting the response-pipe drainer goroutine, so a busy surviving ptyhost's replay (containing real ANSI device queries) blocked Feed forever while holding spawnMu, wedging the whole startup goroutine before ListenAndServe. Root-caused in a prior session (docs/handoff/reattach-deadlock-handoff.md, untracked scratch notes carried over from worktree churn) and DRAFT-patched (docs/handoff/reattach-deadlock-fix.patch); this Sprint verified/applied that patch, extended AC-3 to claude-agent's DiscoverAndRestore, wrote a REALISTIC (>64KiB, real DA1/DA2/CPR queries) regression test that reproduces the deadlock with a demonstrated fail-without-fix / pass-with-fix cycle, and fixed a newly-surfaced pre-existing data race the regression test's realistic throughput exposed.

decisions.decision: Applied docs/handoff/reattach-deadlock-fix.patch as the starting point for internal/tab/claudetui/daemon.go's spawnWithArgs and cmd/palmux/main.go's claudetui.DiscoverAndRestore call, after confirming git apply --check succeeded cleanly against current main (S862203/S64c835 did not touch this region).
decisions.rationale: Patch was already root-caused and reasoned through in a prior session against the exact live code; re-deriving from scratch would duplicate work and risk drifting from the documented analysis. Verified the pre-patch code matched the patch's base context exactly before applying.

decisions.decision: Extended the async-discovery defense (originally patch-drafted for claudetui only) to claudeagent.DiscoverAndRestore's call site in main.go too, via a new shared, named, directly-testable helper runDiscoveryAsync(fn, onResult) rather than two independent inline `go func(){...}()` blocks.
decisions.rationale: AC-Sfeed64-1-3 explicitly requires covering BOTH call sites (the draft patch only covered claudetui; claude-agent got its own synchronous DiscoverAndRestore call in S862203-3 that carries the identical blast-radius risk even though no concrete hang has been found in claudeagent's pipe-mode reattach path yet). A shared named helper (vs. copy-pasted goroutine literals) is directly unit-testable with an injected blocking fn (cmd/palmux/discovery_async_test.go) and gives both call sites one place to fix if the pattern ever needs to change again.

decisions.decision: Built a new fake_claude testdata flag (--query-burst <minBytes>) that emits >64KiB of realistic scrollback filler text interleaved with REAL ANSI device query sequences (DA1 \x1b[c, DA2 \x1b[>c, cursor-position \x1b[6n — the exact three sequences third_party/charmbracelet-x-vt-racefix/handlers.go answers into the emulator's response pipe), used by a two-Daemon reattach scenario (dA spawns fresh + produces the burst as live output; dB, a separately-constructed Daemon over the SAME run dir, reattaches and receives the whole burst as its ATTACH(-1) replay) mirroring the existing TestDaemonReconnectsToSurvivingPtyhostAndRestoresScreen pattern.
decisions.rationale: DESIGN_PRINCIPLES priority-0 rule (added alongside this Sprint's plan commit) requires an AC to reproduce the FAILURE-TRIGGERING condition, not just traverse the code path with toy data — S3f2658's original verification used tens of bytes of query-free heartbeat text and never exercised the response-generating path at all, which is exactly why it shipped broken. A toy poke would not have caught this bug and would not catch a regression of it.

decisions.decision: Added a 500ms delay inside fake_claude's --query-burst handling before the burst starts writing.
decisions.rationale: Initial investigation showed the burst could race dA's OWN first ATTACH(-1) (a fresh spawn's replay is only genuinely empty if the child hasn't produced output yet) — an unlucky race made dA occasionally observe part of the burst as ITS OWN initial replay instead of ordinary live output, which still exercises the same underlying bug but nondeterministically and on the wrong Daemon, undermining the test's intended two-phase (fresh spawn A / reattach B) structure. The delay deterministically lets A's own spawn/attach complete first (normally sub-millisecond) before the burst lands, so the burst reliably becomes B's replay.

decisions.decision: Changed fake_claude's emitQueryBurst to build the entire burst in an in-memory buffer and emit it with ONE os.Stdout.Write call, instead of ~2500 separate small fmt.Fprint calls (one per line/query).
decisions.rationale: The regression test flaked (burst not fully landing within a 30-60s bound) specifically under `go test ./...` full-monorepo parallel load on this 4-core box (many packages' real-subprocess tests competing for CPU simultaneously) — a pre-existing, documented characteristic of this test suite (see internal/tab/claudetui/survival_gate_test.go's doc comment on why heavy real-subprocess tests are gated). Batching into one write call removes ~2500 redundant syscalls without changing the emitted DATA (same size, same content, same interleaved real queries), which resolved the flakiness while preserving full realism.

decisions.decision: Fixed a pre-existing, previously-undetected data race: Daemon.GridSnapshot() and restoreScreenJiggle() called d.emulator.GridSnapshot() without holding feedMu, while vt.SafeEmulator.CellAt returns a *uv.Cell POINTER into its own live buffer under RLock but releases that lock before the caller (cellToGridCell) finishes reading the pointer's fields — a concurrent Feed (write-locked) can mutate the same cell mid-read. Both call sites now go through feedMu, matching the existing pattern already used by RenderSnapshotAndSubscribe for the same class of emulator read.
decisions.rationale: The new realistic-data regression test (high-throughput live Feed calls via readLoop, running concurrently with a reconnect's restoreScreenJiggle -> GridSnapshot call) was the first test in the suite to generate enough concurrent throughput to trip this latent race under `go test -race` — no existing test (all much lower throughput, e.g. --counter-winch's ~10 bytes/100ms) ever exercised it. Per project discipline (no self-judged skips/suppression of real failures, and the explicit AC-Sfeed64-1 requirement not to regress S64c835's -race cleanliness), the race was fixed rather than worked around by weakening the new test's realism.

decisions.decision: AC-Sfeed64-1-4 (real claude-tui session dogfood on green.tjstkm.net, double restart, human-judged) is explicitly NOT attempted by this agent — marked needs_user / escalated.
decisions.rationale: Explicit instruction in the story: this requires a real, human-operated claude-tui session with accumulated conversational output, a real double palmux2 restart on a live host, and human-eyes judgment of screen/conversation continuity — none of which an autonomous agent can safely or meaningfully perform. Also gates the v0.14.13 release per the priority-0 DESIGN_PRINCIPLES rule this same incident produced (no release immediately after 'done' without a real dogfood).

decisions.decision: REVIEW FOLLOW-UP (coordinator, HIGH): the AC-3 change that made startup DiscoverAndRestore async removed the old guarantee — from the previous SYNCHRONOUS discovery calls — that discovery fully completed before st.Run started the 10s scan loop that drives orphan-GC. Added a discovery-completion barrier: new Store.ArmDiscoveryBarrier() returns a release func and installs a `discoveryDone chan struct{}`; gcTuiOrphans and gcAgentOrphans now skip their whole orphan-SHUTDOWN pass (via discoveryGateOpen()) until it is released. main.go arms the barrier BEFORE st.Run and releases it (defer, so success OR failure both release) once discovery finishes. ALSO changed the two discovery passes from two parallel goroutines to ONE sequential goroutine (claude-tui THEN claude-agent), and gated BOTH GCs on the SINGLE barrier.
decisions.rationale: DiscoverAndRestore and both GC passes dial the SAME on-disk ptyhosts — claude-tui and claude-agent share one run dir/seed space in production (both managers resolve to ptyhost.RunDir(prefix); verified in code, and store.gcAgentOrphans's GUARD-RAIL documents it). A GC tick firing while discovery is still mid-adoption of the same surviving orphan socket races: the ptyhost tolerates one connection (Server.replaceConn), and restored Daemons have ResumeOnDeath=true, so a clean orphan SHUTDOWN could flap into a respawn/re-kill (realistic on incus-container workspaces waiting on gateRespawn/container startup). Because the seed space is shared, a per-manager flag (gcTui gated on tui-discovery only, gcAgent on agent-discovery only — the coordinator's first-cut suggestion) would NOT be sufficient: agent-GC gated only on agent-discovery could still race tui-discovery adopting the same socket. Hence ONE barrier covering ALL discovery, and sequential (not parallel) discovery so the two passes do not race each other's socket probes either (the original sync code ran them sequentially; this preserves that ordering while keeping serve unblocked). A discovery that never completes keeps GC deferred forever — the SAFE direction (orphan GC is a cleanup nicety, not correctness-critical; the lazy first-WS-attach path still re-adopts on demand; and the AC-1 root fix means discovery no longer hangs). serve is still never blocked (whole discovery chain is background via runDiscoveryAsync). Barrier field is written once (in Arm, before Run/its goroutine) and read only from the scan goroutine, so no lock guards it; the channel close/receive is the release synchronization (verified -race clean, store -count=2).

decisions.decision: Simplified runDiscoveryAsync from `func(fn func()(int,int,error), onResult func(int,int,error))` to `func(fn func())` now that discovery is one sequential goroutine that does its own logging + barrier release. Updated cmd/palmux/discovery_async_test.go (TestRunDiscoveryAsyncDoesNotBlockCaller) to the new signature — it still pins the same contract (a deliberately-blocking fn does not delay a stand-in ListenAndServe, and the background pass still runs to completion once unblocked).
decisions.rationale: The result-passing plumbing existed only to route per-pass log lines; with both passes and the barrier release living inside one fn closure, the callback was dead weight. The seam (a named, tested `go fn()` wrapper) is kept so a test can assert serve is never blocked and so run() can never accidentally call DiscoverAndRestore synchronously again.

decisions.decision: REVIEW FOLLOW-UP (coordinator, LOW): corrected daemon.go's drainer comments that described the emulator response pipe as a '64KiB buffer' that 'fills'. It is an UNBUFFERED io.Pipe (third_party/charmbracelet-x-vt-racefix/emulator.go: io.Pipe() has zero buffering — a single unread response byte blocks Write). Reworded to say so explicitly and note the fix's correctness relies on the unbuffered semantics (there is no buffer to 'not fill' — the drainer must simply be running before ANY query-answering Feed). Also fixed one test log line that said '64KiB response-pipe threshold' → '>64KiB, AC's realistic not-a-toy floor' (the >64KiB figure is a REPLAY-DATA-SIZE floor from the AC, not a pipe threshold).
decisions.rationale: A future maintainer reading '64KiB buffer' could wrongly conclude a smaller replay is safe or that raising a buffer size would fix it; the truth is any single unread query response blocks, so the ordering (drainer-before-Feed) is the only correct fix. fake_claude.go's comment was already correct and left as-is.

verification.race: go test -race ./internal/tab/claudetui/ — clean; -count=2 clean (coordinator-requested) plus 9 earlier -count=1 runs. go test -race ./internal/store/ -count=2 clean (covers the new discovery barrier: field written pre-Run, read in scan goroutine, channel close = release synchronization).
verification.full_repo: go test ./... — clean across repeated full-suite runs (2 more after the review follow-up). Earlier intermittent flakiness (timing only, not a logic failure) from CPU contention on a 4-core box was resolved by the burst-batching fix (matches survival_gate_test.go's documented, pre-existing rationale for gating heavy real-subprocess tests).
verification.deadlock_reproduction: Confirmed by temporarily reverting ONLY daemon.go's ordering fix (git stash) and re-running the new regression test: (1) with go test's own -timeout, produced a full goroutine dump showing the exact reported production stack (io.(*pipe).write <- PrimaryDeviceAttributes handler <- Emulator.Write <- SafeEmulator.Write (writer lock held) <- claudetui.Emulator.Feed <- daemon.go's pre-fix Feed line <- EnsureStarted (spawnMu held) <- test); (2) after adding the burst-timing delay to deterministically target dB's reattach specifically, produced a clean, self-diagnosing test failure at the internal bound identifying the exact reattach hang. Fix was then restored (git stash pop) and the test re-confirmed passing in ~1s.
verification.discovery_gc_barrier: internal/store/discovery_barrier_test.go TestOrphanGC_DeferredUntilDiscoveryDone: with ArmDiscoveryBarrier armed (discovery in-flight), a gcTuiOrphans+gcAgentOrphans tick is a complete no-op — the fake GCOrphans (which is what dials/SHUTDOWNs orphan sockets) records 0 calls; after release() (discovery done) the next tick records exactly 1 call each; release is idempotent. TestOrphanGC_RunsImmediatelyWithoutBarrier pins the default (nil gate → GC runs immediately) so existing store tests / non-front-loaded deployments are unaffected. PASS.
verification.leaked_processes: none (ps aux checked clean after all test runs)

story_Sfeed64_3_implementation_notes.type: bug fix (found by the green dogfood of Sfeed64-1)
story_Sfeed64_3_implementation_notes.summary: Fixed a dual-manager ptyhost adoption bug surfaced by the green real-machine dogfood of Sfeed64-1: claudetui.DiscoverAndRestore/GCOrphans (internal/tab/claudetui/discover.go's scanRunDir) and claudeagent.DiscoverAndRestore/GCOrphans (internal/tab/claudeagent/discover.go's scanAgentRunDir) both scan the SAME shared ptyhost run dir and, before this fix, treated EVERY identity-bearing (*.sock, *.json) pair found there as their own to dial/adopt/SHUTDOWN — including entries actually owned by the OTHER manager. Since a ptyhost socket tolerates only one live connection at a time (ptyhost.Server.replaceConn evicts the previously-active connection the instant a new one dials in), the two managers evicted each other's connections in a loop on restart, which the daemon side interpreted as session death (SHUTDOWN + respawn), resetting the surviving claude-tui session to a fresh screen even though the system self-healed (no 502). Fixed by using the EXISTING ptyhost.StatusFile.Mode field (already written verbatim from the spawning Config, exactly like the S3f2658-3 explicit-identity fields) as an ownership marker: claudetui's scan now skips (leaves completely untouched — no dial, no adopt, no cleaned-count) any entry whose Mode is ptyhost.ModePipe, and claudeagent's scan symmetrically skips any entry whose Mode is not ptyhost.ModePipe (pty/empty). The check sits immediately after the identity fields are read, BEFORE any liveness dial, in both scanRunDir and scanAgentRunDir — so both DiscoverAndRestore (startup) and GCOrphans (10s orphan-GC piggyback) inherit the fix automatically, since both call the same shared scan function per package.

decisions.decision: Used the pre-existing ptyhost.StatusFile.Mode field (ModePTY/ModePipe, already written by S862203-2/ADR-0004 for an unrelated reason — distinguishing how the ptyhost holds its child process) as the cross-manager ownership marker, rather than inventing a new field (e.g. an explicit 'owner' string in StatusFile).
decisions.rationale: claude-tui always spawns ModePTY (or empty, pre-Mode-field back-compat, also pty) and claude-agent always spawns ModePipe (internal/tab/claudeagent/launch.go) — the mode already encodes ownership 1:1 in production, with zero schema/wire changes needed. This is also literally the marker the S3f2658-3 GUARD-RAIL comment in claudeagent's GCOrphans had anticipated needing but never applied to the on-disk scan (that comment's 'isLive MUST stay mode-agnostic' guidance was about a DIFFERENT, still-valid concern — not asserting tab mode inside the STORE isLive lookup — and remained correct; it just wasn't sufficient on its own, since the destructive step is the DIAL itself, which happens before isLive is ever consulted).

decisions.decision: Placed the Mode check directly inside scanRunDir/scanAgentRunDir, immediately after the explicit RepoID/BranchID/TabID identity fields are validated and BEFORE the skipLive check, the pidAlive check, or the liveness-probe net.Dial+HELLO.
decisions.rationale: The eviction bug is caused by the DIAL itself (ptyhost.Server.replaceConn evicts on any new connection, regardless of who's asking or why) — so the wrong-mode entry must never reach the dial step at all. Filtering inside isLive (a callback GCOrphans receives from the store) would still let scanRunDir/scanAgentRunDir dial the wrong-mode entry during DiscoverAndRestore (which passes skipLive=nil) or during the liveness probe GCOrphans performs before even consulting isLive. Filtering at the single point both discovery and GC share (scanRunDir/scanAgentRunDir) protects both call sites with one change per package, and the wrong-mode entry is left COMPLETELY untouched (not even counted as cleaned — it is not debris).

decisions.decision: Updated the S64c835-3 GUARD-RAIL comment on claudeagent.Manager.GCOrphans, which had asserted the shared-run-dir scan was 'safe ONLY because both are driven by the SAME mode-agnostic isLive' — a claim the green dogfood proved incomplete. The comment now explains the two-layer defense: the Mode filter (this story) keeps wrong-mode entries from ever being dialed/considered, and mode-agnostic isLive (unchanged, still correct) keeps right-mode entries from being wrongly reaped.
decisions.rationale: Leaving a 'this is safe because X' comment standing after X was demonstrated insufficient by a real production incident would mislead a future maintainer. The isLive-must-stay-mode-agnostic guidance itself was not wrong and is preserved verbatim in spirit — a variant that asserted tab MODE inside isLive would still be a real, distinct bug (reaping a referenced ptyhost of the other mode) — but the comment's framing of what makes the shared scan overall safe needed to include the new Mode-filter layer.

decisions.decision: Wrote the AC-Sfeed64-3-2 regression test (cmd/palmux/ptyhost_ownership_test.go, TestPtyOwnership_ModeFilter) in cmd/palmux (package main) rather than inside claudetui or claudeagent, since it is inherently a cross-package scenario requiring BOTH real Managers pointed at the same on-disk run dir — cmd/palmux already imports and wires both in production (main.go), unlike either tab package alone. The test spawns a REAL ptyhost.Server in ModePTY (holding claudetui's testdata/fake_claude.go) and a REAL ptyhost.Server in ModePipe (holding internal/ptyhost/testdata/fake_ndjson.go) in the SAME run dir, then runs claudetui.DiscoverAndRestore and claudeagent.DiscoverAndRestore against it, asserting each adopts exactly ITS OWN entry (adopted=1, cleaned=0 each) and that Manager.Get for the wrong identity returns nil on both sides.
decisions.rationale: AC-Sfeed64-3-2 explicitly requires proving the fix with REAL ptyhosts and BOTH managers' discovery run together against a shared dir, not a synthetic isLive-callback unit test (which the package-local discover_test.go files already cover for the GC path). Reusing the existing fake_claude/fake_ndjson testdata harnesses (rather than inventing new fixtures) keeps the test's child-process behavior identical to the packages' own suites.

decisions.decision: The regression test's Go test function name is deliberately short (TestPtyOwnership_ModeFilter) and its ptyhost run dir uses a dedicated os.MkdirTemp('', 'sfeed64-3-own') rather than testing.T.TempDir(), instead of the more conventional t.TempDir().
decisions.rationale: testing.T.TempDir() embeds the full (sub)test name in its generated path. A first draft with a long, descriptive test name (TestOwnershipModeFilter_TuiAdoptsPTY_AgentAdoptsPipe_NeitherAdoptsBoth, 70 chars) combined with cmd/palmux's own t.TempDir() nesting produced socket paths over 108 bytes, the AF_UNIX sun_path limit on Linux (dial failed with 'invalid argument' before the test even reached its assertions) — the exact class of bug ptyhost.FileKey's doc comment already warns about for RunDir itself. Renaming the test function and switching to a short, manually-managed temp dir (with its own t.Cleanup(os.RemoveAll)) fixed it deterministically rather than relying on the ambient temp-dir prefix staying short.

decisions.decision: Manually verified the regression test's bug-catching power by temporarily disabling both Mode-filter checks (replacing each `if sf.Mode == ...ModePipe { continue }` body with `if false { continue }`), confirming TestPtyOwnership_ModeFilter FAILS with 'claudetui adopted = 2, want 1' and log output showing the EXACT failure signature from the dogfood report (subprocess died unexpectedly / resume-on-death disabled / broken pipe / bad json line), then restoring the real fix and re-confirming PASS. This was a manual before/after comparison, not committed as a toggle in the source.
decisions.rationale: AC-Sfeed64-3-2 explicitly requires demonstrating the test fails without the fix. Doing this by hand (temporary local edit, run, revert) rather than shipping a build-tag/env-var toggle keeps the committed fix minimal and avoids adding permanent dead-code branches whose only purpose is a one-time demonstration.

verification.regression_test: cmd/palmux/ptyhost_ownership_test.go TestPtyOwnership_ModeFilter: PASS with the fix (tuiAdopted=1, agentAdopted=1, cleaned=0/0, cross-adoption checks via Manager.Get all nil, adopted pty Daemon's pid unchanged from the pre-existing ptyhost's pid). Manually confirmed FAIL (tuiAdopted=2) with the Mode filter disabled, reproducing the dogfood's eviction/respawn log signature exactly, then restored the fix and re-confirmed PASS.
verification.leaked_processes: none (ps aux checked clean after test runs; temporary demonstration repro tool and binaries removed from the tree before commit)
